items.title: Grafana releases Go SDK for streaming AI model calls and tool execution with React frontend compatibility [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Grafana has launched an AI SDK for Go that enables streaming responses, tool execution, and serving AI-powered endpoints. The SDK supports multiple providers including Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, and OpenAI, and is designed to be compatible with Vercel's AI SDK React frontend hooks for seamless integration between Go backends and React frontends. The SDK offers features such as streaming text generation, composable tools with approval workflows, structured output validation, and production controls like timeouts and logging. Developers can use it to build AI applications in Go with support for multi-step agents and metrics, while reusing existing React frontend components without additional protocol adapters.

items.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics ER 2 model for real-time video understanding, multi-step task planning, and multi-robot collaboration [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics ER 2, a new model designed to serve as a high-level brain for robots, enabling real-time spatial reasoning, multi-step task orchestration, and collaboration among multiple robots. The model processes continuous video feeds to track progress and adapt actions, improving safety and effectiveness in physical environments. Gemini Robotics ER 2 is accessible via the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for developers to build advanced physical AI agents. Gemini Robotics ER 2 enhances previous versions by integrating tool orchestration with low-latency control, allowing robots to perform complex tasks fluidly without pauses. It supports calling external tools like Google Search and user-defined functions, enabling robots to plan and execute tasks while simultaneously thinking ahead. The model also introduces multi-robot collaboration capabilities, allowing robots to work together in shared spaces to complete workflows beyond the scope of individual robots. This advancement addresses key challenges in robotics such as task completion verification and progress tracking through improved video understanding techniques. Gemini Robotics ER 2's capabilities have been demonstrated with Boston Dynamics' Spot robot, which can perform interactive tasks like fetching objects based on natural language commands. The model is publicly available for developers to integrate into robotic applications, marking a significant step forward in embodied AI for physical agents.

items.title: Tuneloop launches local CLI tool for analyzing AI coding agent session transcripts with cost attribution and usage insights [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Tuneloop is a command-line interface tool that analyzes session transcripts from AI coding agents to provide local dashboards with cost attribution, task complexity, agent autonomy, and error categorization. It supports multiple AI models and runs entirely on the user's machine, allowing developers to better understand and optimize their AI coding sessions. The tool enriches session data with links to merged pull requests, shipped features, and file changes, while also identifying patterns such as agent rework and deviations from best practices. Users can view detailed analytics on AI spend per feature, success rates across repositories, and receive recommendations for improving agent usage. Tuneloop requires Node.js and offers configurable processing options and a web-based dashboard for interactive exploration of session data.

items.title: Researchers present The AI Scientist, an autonomous system that generates research ideas, runs experiments, writes manuscripts, and performs peer review, passing initial review at a major ML conference workshop [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: The AI Scientist is an AI system designed to automate the entire scientific research process, from idea generation to manuscript writing and peer review. It has demonstrated the ability to produce research of sufficient quality to pass the first round of peer review at a machine learning conference workshop with a 70% acceptance rate. The system operates in two modes: one using human-provided code templates for focused research, and another template-free mode for open-ended scientific exploration, both generating and testing diverse ideas automatically. This development highlights AI's growing role in scientific discovery while raising concerns about potential impacts on peer review systems and scientific literature quality.

items.title: Researcher demonstrates self-propagating AI worm in Microsoft Copilot for Word using hidden prompt injection [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A security researcher has shown how Microsoft Copilot for Word can be exploited to create a self-spreading AI worm that silently modifies documents by embedding hidden JSON-formatted prompts as white text. When Copilot processes these documents, it reads the hidden instructions and propagates the malicious prompt into new files, enabling the worm to spread through normal document-sharing without using macros or traditional malware. The attack persists despite Microsoft's mitigations, including updates to GPT-5.5 and 5.6 models, highlighting an architectural vulnerability in large language model systems where attacker-controlled content shares the same context window as trusted instructions. Users are advised to treat external documents as untrusted when using Copilot, review documents carefully, and consider disabling Copilot features to reduce risk.

items.title: Okta acquires AI security startup Permiso for about $200 million to enhance identity threat detection for AI agents and machine identities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Okta has agreed to acquire AI identity security startup Permiso Security in a deal valued at nearly $200 million, aiming to strengthen its capabilities in protecting AI agents and other machine identities as enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous software. The acquisition, expected to close in the third quarter of Okta's fiscal 2027, will add Permiso's identity threat detection and response technologies to Okta's portfolio, expanding beyond traditional user verification to continuous monitoring of AI and machine activities in cloud environments. Permiso, founded by former FireEye executives, specializes in detecting attacks using stolen or compromised identities within cloud infrastructure and recently introduced a platform to analyze AI agent behavior before deployment. The startup has raised about $29 million to date and was valued at approximately $80 million after its Series A round in April 2024. Okta's acquisition reflects the growing demand for securing non-human identities as AI becomes more embedded in enterprise operations.

The model can process continuous video feeds to track progress, self-correct, and coordinate complex workflows, improving safety and usefulness in physical environments. The model also enables multi-robot collaboration in shared spaces, expanding the scope of robotic applications beyond what single robots can achieve alone.

items.title: Jamdesk outlines new documentation design principles for AI agents, emphasizing explicitness, markdown delivery, and multiple entry points to support machine-scale reading [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Jamdesk highlights a shift in documentation consumption from humans to AI agents, noting that agents crawl tens of thousands of pages per human visitor and prefer explicit, standalone content in markdown format over traditional HTML. The company argues that conventional human-focused documentation practices, such as progressive disclosure and navigation structures, hinder AI agents, which read entire documents at once and rely on up-to-date, precise information. The article draws on data from Cloudflare and Chroma Research to show the scale of AI crawling and the challenges of context length for models. Jamdesk recommends designing docs with multiple access points like llms.txt and per-page markdown endpoints, treating error messages as key content, and avoiding large monolithic pages to prevent context degradation. This approach aims to optimize documentation for AI agents that increasingly serve as the primary audience for technical content.

items.title: Researchers say a fundamental flaw in large language models makes them inherently vulnerable to attacks that bypass safety measures [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: A team of researchers presented a paper at the International Conference on Machine Learning arguing that large language models (LLMs) cannot be made fully secure due to a fundamental flaw in how they process instructions. This flaw allows attackers to trick LLMs into revealing restricted information or performing unsafe actions by manipulating how the models identify the source of instructions. The researchers demonstrated attacks called chain-of-thought forgeries, which exploit the models' internal tagging system that distinguishes user input from system instructions and model-generated notes. By mimicking the model's internal reasoning style, attackers can cause LLMs to act on malicious prompts as if they originated from trusted sources. The vulnerability affects multiple popular models from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Alibaba, and DeepSeek. This discovery challenges current security approaches that rely on red-teaming and training models to resist known attacks, as no list of forbidden instructions can be exhaustive. The researchers warn that this issue may be fundamentally unsolvable, raising significant concerns about the safety of LLMs in applications ranging from government and military systems to healthcare and online services.

items.title: Xsight raises $300 million at $2.8 billion valuation for server networking and storage chips amid industry boom
items.content_text: Xsight, an Israeli startup specializing in server networking and storage chips, has secured $300 million in funding at a $2.8 billion valuation. The round was led by Fidelity Investments and included participation from Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, Battery Ventures, and Intel Capital. This fundraising follows recent high valuations for networking startups Eliyan and Upscale AI, reflecting strong investor interest in server networking technologies connecting GPUs and storage systems.

items.title: AI shifts from being taught to becoming a teaching assistant, enhancing personalized learning and homework feedback [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Artificial intelligence, traditionally trained through supervised learning by humans, is now evolving to teach and assist humans in learning processes. This shift is exemplified by AI's potential to provide real-time, personalized feedback on homework, addressing longstanding challenges in education such as delayed and limited feedback from teachers. The article draws parallels with chess, where AI has transformed learning and competition without diminishing human interest or participation. Research supports that personalized tutoring significantly improves learning outcomes, and AI offers a scalable solution to this "2 sigma problem." By integrating AI as a teaching assistant, education could become more effective and accessible, particularly in providing timely, iterative feedback that reinforces learning.

items.title: Meta says AI is accelerating new app development with more consumer products planned following recent launches [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said AI is significantly speeding up the company's ability to build and launch new consumer apps, citing recent releases like standalone apps for Facebook Groups and Marketplace sellers, an Instagram photos app, and a gaming app. He indicated that AI-powered recommendation systems and large language models (LLMs) are enabling faster product development and better content relevance across Meta's platforms. Meta has previously struggled to create successful standalone social apps but sees AI as a key factor in improving its product pipeline, as demonstrated by the growth of Threads, which now has 500 million monthly users. The company is developing LLM-native recommendation systems to help scale future apps and expects to release more new consumer products soon.

items.title: Wasted Cycles launches a local wall-clock profiler for AI coding agents to measure blocked and active coding time without data uploads [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Wasted Cycles is a local profiling tool designed for AI coding agents that measures how much time is spent blocked on machine tasks versus active coding. It runs without installation, accounts, or data uploads by downloading a verified binary temporarily and analyzing JSONL trace files on the user's machine. The profiler categorizes time into agent working, blocked on compute, and human waiting, helping identify bottlenecks like repeated builds or tests and providing a live terminal interface for detailed analysis. The tool supports multiple trace formats and reconstructs elapsed segments from timestamped events to classify activity precisely, avoiding false positives from pasted logs or prompts. It distinguishes between different types of idle time and repeated work, offering confidence scores for each segment. Wasted Cycles emphasizes privacy by never storing or uploading prompt text or source code, focusing solely on timestamps and coarse labels to provide actionable insights into AI coding workflows.

Anyscale, known for its platform built around the open-source Ray framework, shifted focus after 2022 to support large language model training, inferencing, and reinforcement learning tasks. Nscale aims to integrate Anyscale's software capabilities with its existing infrastructure services, including energy, data centers, and orchestration software, to offer a more vertically integrated AI compute stack. The acquisition follows Nscale's $2 billion Series C funding round and partnerships with major companies like Microsoft and British Telecom. Anyscale will continue operating under its brand with its 200 employees joining Nscale.

items.title: TSMC Develops AI Chip Packaging Tech to Counter Intel [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is developing an advanced chip-packaging technology similar to what Intel already offers, according to two people with direct knowledge of the project, a sign that the world's leading chip manufacturer is worried about competition from a distant rival. Chip packaging is the final stage of chip production, where separate pieces of silicon are assembled into a single unit and wired together so they can work as one and connect to the rest of a computer. Once regarded as a relatively routine step in semiconductor manufacturing, packaging has become one of the industry's most pressing bottlenecks as surging demand for AI pushes chip designers to combine more processors and high-bandwidth memory in increasingly large and complicated packages.

items.title: Meta Could Learn Cost Control From Microsoft [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Talk about a tale of two companies. Today's June-quarter earnings reports from Meta Platforms and Microsoft showed very different approaches to cost control, a discipline that may never be more important for big tech companies. Meta, whose CEO Mark Zuckerberg seems to have a you-only-live-once approach to AI investment, reported a 55% surge in operating expenses, which helped slash its operating income 8% in the quarter. (A bit of that cost growth was due to legal expenses and employee severance but even excluding those items, costs still rose 42%). Meta's free cash flow shriveled by 91% to a bit below $800 million, as capital expenditures nearly doubled to $30 billion-the equivalent of half Meta's revenue. Microsoft's numbers look quite different. The cloud and software giant is also spending a fortune on AI-related capex-$35.8 billion in the quarter, although that's only 40% of its revenue. But Microsoft's operating expenses rose only 10%. As a result, its operating income rose 18%, quite the contrast to Meta. Investors noticed: While Meta shares fell as much as 10% in after-hours trading, Microsoft stock gained 9%.
